messages:
jordan: opening this thread after noisy alerts around 11:07 UTC — client SDKs reported repeated retries and we saw TLS handshake failures for cross-region egress (us-east -> eu-west). posting initial findings and action owners here.
li: alerted at 11:09. dashboard: retry-rate climbed to ~3.4% for ~12m, spike coincides with a routing update from the control plane at 11:02.
carla: logs show a cluster of `alert unexpected_message` and `certificate verify failed: certificate has expired or is not yet valid` from a subset of edges. but certs on disk look valid — suspect mismatch between SNI thumbprint and the serving instance.
nate: grabbed a quick pcap from an affected host:
```
11:06:58.212345 IP proxies-us-east > edge-eu: Flags [S], seq 0, win 64240
11:06:58.212900 IP edge-eu > proxies-us-east: Flags [R], seq 0, win 0
11:07:01.123456 TLS  edge-eu: handshake failure: server cert CN mismatch, sent cert with CN=edge-legacy.local
```
jordan: hypothesis: during a recent rolling egress patch the routing table briefly pointed traffic at a legacy edge pool that retained an old cert/template. clients attempted connection, got a cert that didn't match SNI -> TLS fail -> SDK retried aggressively causing downstream amplification.
li: immediate mitigations we ran at 11:12: 1) temporarily pin routing for cross-region egress to the stable pool 2) drained suspected legacy pool 3) triggered a config reload on all edge nodes in eu-west. errors dropped to baseline by 11:28.
carla: triage call notes and action items (owner / ETA):
  - jordan -> audit routing-policy history and remove all references to legacy-edge pools; add an explicit deny for deprecated pool IDs (ETA 2026-04-04)
  - li -> add an automated post-rollout cert+SNI consistency check in the control-plane job (ETA 2026-03-29)
  - nate -> instrument an SNI-thumbprint mismatch counter + alert (ETA 2026-03-27)
  - carla -> update incident runbook with a clear path: pin, drain, invalidate cache, and smoke-check (ETA 2026-03-26)
  - ops-bot -> create a recurring reliability review item to track cross-region refires (RH-4021) (ETA immediate)
ops-bot: created ticket RH-4021 (internal/rh/4021) and assigned to jordan,li,nate,carla. status=open.
jordan: my cleanup plan: 1) generate a PR that removes legacy pool entries from the global routing map 2) add a CI check that fails on dangling pool references 3) run a controlled prune on Wednesday. will post RH-4021 updates here.
li: plan for control-plane check: after any routing change, run a short probe that does a TLS handshake per-pop and validates server_name => cert CN and SANs. will include results in the rollout summary.
nate: quick probe snippet I'll PR for telemetry export:
```
python -c "import ssl,socket; s=ssl.create_default_context();
conn=s.wrap_socket(socket.socket(), server_hostname='api.redwood.example'); conn.connect(('edge-eu',443)); print(conn.getpeercert())"
```
carla: runbook reminder: Dedicated/Private environments use a slightly different templating system. confirm that the deny/cleanup doesn't accidentally drop private pools. adding a verification step in the runbook.
jordan: recurring pattern note: ops observed 4 similar small-scale routing->TLS incidents in the last year; grouping them in RH-4021 for trend analysis and mitigations.
li: proposed longer-term mitigations:
  - add route-change safeguards: short suppress window and verification probe before propagating to all regions
  - tie canary gating to an SNI-consistency metric so we fail fast on template/cert skews
  - implement client SDK soft cap and jitter during cross-region recoveries to reduce amplification
carla: scheduling a 25min follow-up sync Friday 09:00 UTC to split RH-4021 into concrete PRs and owners. invite will include runbook diff and example probes.
jordan: owners please prefix progress updates with "RH-4021" in this thread so the ops-bot annotates tickets. I'll close RH-4021 when route cleanup PR merged, control-plane check live, and SNI alerting in place.
net-bot: post-mitigation health: retry-rate back to 0.6% by 11:35; monitoring for recurrence. next_check=2026-03-27T10:00:00Z.
